# Application tabs

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:application-tabs` · Kerf UI · CSS composition · Navigation

Controlled document tabs with application-owned state and panels.

## When to use

Show AppTab and TabBar in a complete controlled composition.

- Compose application state, panels, actions, overflow, and reordering around TabBar and AppTab.

**Not when:**

- Use SegmentedControl instead for a compact local choice.

## Imports

- Nothing to import: this is a reference composition.
- Declared side effects: css.

## Props

No props: this entry has no JavaScript API.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- overflow
- keyboard and pointer reordering
- adding and closing documents

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.
- Built from: [AppTab](./tabs.md), [TabBar](./tab-bar.md), [ToolbarControlGroup](./toolbar-control-group.md), [Text](./text.md), [Card](./wa-card.md).

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** ordered tabs; selected tab; tabpanels; add and close policy; routing and persistence.

No wiring helper.

## Geometry

Margin: child · border: child · padding: child (layout role: navigation). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

## Accessibility

- Keep one selected tab synchronized with one named tabpanel and retain the wireTabBars disposer.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and forced component dimensions (`KUI-L005`).
